title: Few new records and listening to them on the road
summary: Ten new records a month was a lot then; he could not afford a phonograph on the road and listened when at home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Musicians listen to those records a lot I guess.
Yeah. They -- they don't get very many records during the year like the market is flooded with records now.
But inthem days, if ten records came out a month -- ten new records came out a month, it was
doing great you know. Now they got so many records coming out every month, you can't keep up with them.
A lot of things get lost that way too.
But I guess if a new Louis Hot Five or Hot Seven came out something like that -- everbody would listen to it.
Because just solos -- you know some of them by heart.
Yeah, I used to listen -- I used to keep my ears open you know.
Did you carry a phonograph with you on the road and --
Oh, no. I couldn't afford a phonograph.
So when did you listen to records?
Whenever I got a chance to.
Like if you went to somebody's house or something --
Whever I was at home I used to get records -- buy records. Sit around and hear the record.
